newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down vs dollar in tight-range trade.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down vs dollar in tight-range trade.

text.p: The ringgit was weaker against the dollar for most of Friday's session as rates were again locked in a tight trading range, dealers said.

The ringgit edged up slightly after Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he saw no immediate need to lower interest rates to spur the economy. But the rise quickly fizzled out as players were reluctant to take fresh positions ahead of the weekend and the release of U.S. non-farm payrolls data at 1330 GMT.
The local currency stayed firm against the Singapore dollar on the back of rising dollar/Sing. The Singapore dollar hit a 17-month low against the U.S. currency on Friday.

"Movement in ringgit/Sing seen as straight dollar/Sing play so far, but of course, it is possible that the second leg would hit the dollar/ringgit later," research house MMS International said in its market commentary.
Dealers said U.S. hedge funds were going into the ringgit/Sing cross for its yield and Malaysia's strong economic fundamentals.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4802/12 a dollar against 2.4736/46 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.
The Singapore dollar was at 1.7293/12 ringgit from 1.7295/15.
